newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark edges closer to 1.80 after Kohl comments.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark edges closer to 1.80 after Kohl comments.

text.p: The dollar edged closer to 1.80 marks at midday Europe, testing session highs after German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said the recent strength in the dollar against the mark was not earth-shaking.

Dealers said the comments underlined the German government's apparent tolerance of the dollar's latest bout of strength against the mark, but heavy offers above around and above the key 1.80 level were still seen hampering gains above there.
Chancellor Kohl's comments enlivened an otherwise dull day with a market starved for fresh factors to provide dollar direction.

Chancellor Kohl said people used to complain when dollar weakness hit German exports. "Now things are going a bit the other way, which is not earth-shaking, it does not mean we should start moaning again," he said.
By 1058 GMT, dollar/mark was trading at 1.7977/82 marks after touching a high of 1.7997 after Kohl's remarks. The dollar stood around 1.7930 pre-Kohl and 1.7920/25 late Thursday.

Dealers said the comments were similar to official statements from the German government earlier in the week that short-term currency fluctuations were not a worry and there was no reason to dramatise recent forex developments.

Earlier, the market took little notice of a slight rise in German research institute Ifo's West German business climate index, up to 96 in June from 95.4 in May and against median expectations of around 95.7.
Analysts said the rise reflected the growth in exports and the weaker mark but the data gave little indication of Germany's muted domestic growth and unemployment situation.

"Germany's output sector is in recovery, it's when they start employing someone that will make a bigger difference to the economy," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International. "This data doesn't pose any risk of inflation."

The mark firmed slightly on its European crosses, encouraged by the dollar's failure to clear 1.80 marks. Caution before France's public accounts audit on Monday, which is seen potentially upsetting Europe's monetary union timetable also helped underpin the mark.
Against the yen, the dollar ticked closer to 116 from earlier lows around the mid-115 region.
Dollar/yen was trading at 115.80/85, above early lows of 115.43 but still shy of late Thursday's late European level of 116.00/05.
